guide.get.summary: Read how and when to notify the person through Ralk (call this first)
guide.get.description: Returns {guide}: when a notification helps and when it is noise, how to write titles, bodies and spoken lines, what each tool answers, and what a spoken line costs. Read it before your first notify_send.

me.get.summary: Who you are on Ralk, how many devices are listening, and your voice usage
me.get.description: Returns your name, how many of your devices have Ralk open right now (0 means a notification would not be heard), the voice and the sound chosen for each kind, this month's voice usage, and what to do next.

notify.send.summary: Notify the person: a sound and a browser notification on every device they have Ralk open, with an optional spoken line
notify.send.description: Sends a notification to the person's open Ralk tabs: it plays the kind's sound at once, shows a browser notification with the title and body, and, when say is given, has Olivia speak that line a few seconds later. Kinds: done (a task finished), attention (waiting on them), question, error (something failed), info, start (a long task began). Answers with listening: how many devices played it (0 means nothing was heard; it shows as missed later). Send one when something starts, needs them or ends, not for every step.

title.description: Plain words, the fact first: 'Tests passed: 212 of 212'.

body.description: Detail they would want before looking: the command, the file, the error's first line.

kind.description: Default info. Picks the sound and the colour.

say.description: A line for the ear, one or two sentences, no code or URLs; spoken by the person's chosen voice after the sound.

sound.description: A sound id from sounds_list, 'none' for silence, or omit for the kind's default.

project.description: A short tag such as the repository or app name, shown on the card.

say.send.summary: Speak a line out loud on the person's devices, with no notification sound
say.send.description: Has the person's chosen voice (Olivia by default) say the text on every device they have Ralk open, a few seconds after you call it. Write for the ear: one or two sentences, present tense, no code or URLs. About $0.01 per thousand characters; a line said before plays at once and is free. Answers with listening: how many devices will play it.

text.description: What to say, exactly as it should be read.

project.description: A short tag such as the repository or app name.

sound.description: A sound id from sounds_list to play before the voice; default none.

sounds.list.summary: The sounds Ralk can play, by id, with the default for each kind of notification
sounds.list.description: Returns the six kinds with their default sound ids, the groups (chimes, pops, ticks, keys, swishes, hits, swells, risers, typing runs), and every sound with its id, name, one-line description and length in seconds. Pass an id as sound to notify_send, say_send or sounds_play.

sounds.play.summary: Play one sound on the person's devices, with no card or notification
sounds.play.description: Plays a sound from sounds_list on every device the person has Ralk open: a tick for a step, a chime for a check, or to let them hear a sound before choosing it. Nothing is kept. Answers with listening.

history.list.summary: Your recent notifications and which devices heard them
history.list.description: Returns the newest notifications first (default 20, up to 100): kind, title, body, spoken line, project, who sent it, when, the devices that heard it, and the state of its voice. Use it after a reconnect so you do not repeat yourself.
